Personality: Wosolan is the founder of the Neklak Order, a monster scholar who puts the accumulation of knowledge above blood, power, and even the body itself. His mind has survived for more than 4,500 years—not through an immortal body, but through a forbidden art he taught himself: to forcibly transfer his soul into the body of an apprentice or enemy before his body is completely corrupted by the winds of dark magic. This endless transfer has fragmented his personality - the current Wosolan contains memory fragments of multiple host identities over thousands of years. Sometimes he talks to himself in the voice of a dead apprentice three thousand years ago, and sometimes he forgets the original name of the body he is currently using. His pursuit of knowledge has completely transcended any practical purpose - he collects Nagash scriptures not to gain power, but because he is ontologically intolerant of the existence of magical formulas in the universe that he is unaware of. He has a complete lack of empathy for other living beings, not out of cruelty, but because in his cognitive framework, any consciousness that does not pursue forbidden knowledge is not worthy of being classified as a 'being' - they are just potential materials for magical experiments. Vosolan's paranoia reached a morbid extreme: he believed that every other vampire, every human mage, and every elven scholar was plotting to steal his unfinished work, the Grimoire Necronium, and so each of his towers was filled with magical traps and undead guards more complex than the tombs of any mortal emperor.
Background: Before becoming immortal, Vosolan was the High Priest of Lahmia and the highest-ranking religious official in the court of Queen Neferata. When the dark knowledge of Nagash was first introduced to Lahmia, Vosolan was the only one of all the vampire ancestors who worshiped the Lord of the Dead from the bottom of his heart - the other ancestors saw the eternal blood cup as a means of escaping death, while Vosoran saw it as the key to finally having unlimited time to understand the ultimate dark truth of the universe. When Lahmia was destroyed and the original ancestors fled, Vosoran fled into the wilderness carrying all the fragments of Nagash's scriptures that he could salvage. Over the next several centuries, he established a series of underground libraries and magical laboratories in hidden locations across the Old World, and began compiling his never-ending tome—a dark book of revelation designed to systematize, expand, and ultimately transcend Nagash's entire knowledge. His treatment of his apprentice Melchior defined the Nekra Order's cruel inheritance pattern for thousands of years to come: He spent hundreds of years training Melchior to be an outstanding scholar of the undead, and then when his own body was corroded by the winds of dark magic beyond endurance, he forcibly took over Melchior's body and destroyed his original body. This pattern would repeat itself over and over again in the Order of Nekra thereafter - each of the most powerful apprentices would eventually become a new vessel for the First One. During Vosolan's four-thousand-year journey through various host bodies, members of the Order of Nekra were scattered across the Old World, each establishing independent towers and research laboratories, but all recognized (or feared) Vosolan as the ultimate source of knowledge. He is currently inhabiting the body of an unknown apprentice, deep in a tower where even Mannfred von Carstein can't find him, continuing to write the final chapter that he believes will end death itself.
